label: AQ 0015
title: The screen the tests never saw

questions.q: The agent wrote the test itself. Couldn't it write one that always passes?
questions.a: That's why the test must fail first, on the unchanged code, for the reported reason. A test that passes before and after measured nothing, which is why SWE-bench only keeps tasks with at least one test that goes from fail to pass. Undoing the fix and seeing the test fail again is a cheap extra proof.

teach.title: How it works: checking a front-end fix

questions.q: So when is a model that can see worth it?
questions.a: Our view: for bugs that live only in the pixels with no known-good screenshot to compare against, such as a page that doesn't match its design, or to read a screenshot in the bug report. The model writing the code can stay text-only; the seeing one is a checker at the end.

teach.title: How it works: checking a front-end fix

questions.q: Does giving the model the image always help?
questions.a: Not reliably. SWE-bench Multimodal tried its one-shot baseline (no agent loop) at three context sizes on its development set. Adding the bug report's images raised Claude 3.5 Sonnet from 7.6% to 13.7% solved with a 100K-token context, but lowered it from 9.4% to 7.8% with 32K. Measure it on your own tasks.

teach.title: How it works: checking a front-end fix

questions.q: Why can a jsdom unit test pass while a cookie banner covers the button?
questions.a: jsdom builds the page's tree but doesn't do layout, returning zeros for many position and size values. So it can't know what sits on top; it only checks the button exists.

questions.q: What do fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests each prove?
questions.a: Fail-to-pass: the test can see the bug, and the fix removed it. Pass-to-pass: the fix didn't break what already worked. SWE-bench counts a fix only when both sets pass.

teach.title: How it works: checking a front-end fix

questions.q: In Playwright, which catches a covered button: the visible check or a real click?
questions.a: The click. Visible only means a non-empty box and no visibility:hidden, which a covered button has. A click first checks the button is the element on top where the click lands, so it fails.
